original_ask: We're finding new supporters for FundaMental Health. Apollo generates the segmented prospect list (5 talk-track segments), and Klaviyo runs the touchpoints/sequences after that. The team needs a system an intern can run to bridge the two: research each Apollo-generated prospect and personalize outreach before it goes into Klaviyo. Live API integration with both Apollo and Klaviyo is required for the hackathon demo, and the team is standing up demo/test accounts for both.

confirmed_intent.outcome: A local web app for the AI Donor Outreach Agent: pulls the Apollo-generated, segmented prospect list via live API, has AI research each prospect and draft a personalized talk-track-matched email, puts it in an intern review queue for edit/approve, then pushes the approved contact/draft into Klaviyo via live API to run the touchpoint sequence.
confirmed_intent.actor: Development Associate / Fundraising Intern (primary); Director of Development, Executive Director, Major Gifts Officer (secondary).
confirmed_intent.problem: Someone currently has to manually research each Apollo-generated prospect and hand-pick/personalize the right talk track before anything goes into Klaviyo -- that manual step is the bottleneck this removes.
confirmed_intent.why_now: AI Trailblazer San Diego hackathon (2026-08-01) -- judging rewards real shipped artifacts and real outreach in motion, not a spec document.
confirmed_intent.success: A live demo where a judge watches the app pull a handful of real prospects (2-3+, not the full ~50) from Apollo, generate research + a draft, get approved, and land as a real contact/touchpoint in Klaviyo -- a working closed loop.
confirmed_intent.constraint: Must use live Apollo + Klaviyo API integration (not CSV handoff) against demo/test accounts currently being created. Klaviyo API access is low-risk (private API key, no plan-tier gating found). Apollo API access carries real risk: advanced API access appears gated to the Organization tier ($119/mo, 3-seat minimum) on some sources, and exports consume credits (Free tier only 10/month) -- a Free Apollo account is likely to block the live-pull half of the integration, so a paid tier may be required before the demo.
confirmed_intent.out_of_scope: Auto-send without approval, follow-up sequences, phone calls, donation negotiation, advanced CRM automation, grant-proposal generation (separate Grant Scoping Tool track).

discovery_notes: Apollo generates a segmented list ("next best 50 supporters") across 5 talk-track segments: community donors (mental health affinity), nonprofit/marketing professionals, potential board members, financial institutions with CRA obligations, DAF advisors and giving circle organizers.
Klaviyo runs the actual touchpoint sequences after Apollo generates the list -- confirmed by the team as the current (manual) pipeline this tool automates the middle of.

An existing informal PRD (PRD_AI_Donor_Outreach_Agent.docx, and a hackathon-updated draft at docs/supporters/PRD_AI_Donor_Outreach_Agent_v1.1_hackathon.md) already describes this workflow (research -> draft -> human review -> send) and an AI Behavior Spec (human-in-the-loop required, no fabrication, confidence indicators, approved-sources-only) -- this governs AI behavior for the build regardless of platform specifics.

API investigation completed: Klaviyo uses private API key auth (Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key), profile create/update via POST /api/profile-import, list membership via the Lists API -- no plan-tier gating found. Apollo uses API key auth (x-api-key header, created in Settings > Integrations), but sources conflict on Free-tier API access and 'advanced API access' is explicitly an Organization-tier feature; exports consume credits (Free tier = 10/month).

No existing Apollo/Klaviyo credentials found locally -- only generic Composio app-catalog cache entries (~/.composio/apps/APOLLO, ~/.composio/apps/KLAVIYO), not real keys, and the composio CLI isn't installed. Composio ships pre-built Apollo/Klaviyo actions (contact sync, list/segment ops, event triggers) that could shortcut the integration if the team connects real accounts through it instead of raw REST calls.

Real, sourced (non-fabricated) sample prospect data already researched for all 5 talk-track segments as test fixtures: ~123 named prospects total across segment-01 through segment-05 markdown files in the scratchpad -- useful as realistic seed data before live Apollo access is confirmed.

Open question raised in the team's own notes but not resolved by us: "why have an intern review and approve?" -- kept as a hard requirement per the existing PRD's compliance and hallucination-prevention rationale; flagged for the team to explicitly revisit with Mychal rather than decided unilaterally here.
questions_for_grill: Apollo's Organization-tier API gating ($119/mo) is a real cost/timing risk for the hackathon window -- should the plan build in a CSV-export fallback (matching the original PRD's V1 Apollo import step) if a paid tier can't be secured in time, or is live pull a hard blocker with no fallback?

Should the app integrate directly against Apollo/Klaviyo REST APIs, or through Composio's pre-built actions (faster to wire up, but adds a third-party dependency and requires installing/configuring the composio CLI)?

Where does talk-track segment matching actually happen -- does Apollo's generated list already tag each prospect with one of the 5 segments, or does the app need to infer/assign a segment from raw prospect fields (title, company, etc.)?

What does the review-queue UI need to be usable in a live demo (single list view vs. per-prospect detail view, inline edit vs. regenerate button, any keyboard shortcuts for speed)? Not yet specified by the team.

Should the Klaviyo push only create/update a profile, or also directly trigger a specific flow per talk track -- which would require mapping each of the 5 talk tracks to a corresponding Klaviyo flow ID ahead of the demo?
